## Questions

**Q1.** With measles outbreaks in Maryland and other states, you want to explore how kindergarten vaccine exemptions have changed in each Maryland jurisdiction since before the COVID-19 pandemic. Except a map is probably not the best way to show changes in two numbers for 24 places. Let's make a chart instead, and the type is up to you, but the goal is to clearly show the differences between the 2018-2019 and 2023-2024 school years.

You MUST do the following things when answering this question: \* Load the md_kindergarten_county_2018.csv and md_kindergarten_county_2023.csv files from the data folder \* Join those dataframes, specifying the join column. (Hint: look closely at the County column in each file before deciding which column to join on.) \* Add columns showing the change in the religious exemption rate and the change in the MMR vaccination rate between the two school years. \* Export that joined dataframe to a CSV file using `write_csv`. \* Using that exported CSV, make a chart with Datawrapper. What kind of chart is up to you, so experiment with a few kinds of charts to see what answers the question above in the clearest way. Your chart MUST: \* Have a title, description and source that tells readers about the data. The title and description should highlight the most newsworthy or important aspect. \* Easily readable labels and values \* Publish your chart \* Describe your thought process below - why you chose to make the chart you did - and add the URL of your chart.

**Q2.** You're interested in seeing how flu vaccination rates in Maryland have changed since before the pandemic for different age groups. The `md_flu_vax_by_age.csv` file, from the CDC's FluVaxView program, has the estimated percentage of Marylanders in each age group who had gotten a flu shot by the end of each month of the flu season, for three seasons: 2019-20, 2022-23 and 2025-26. The month column is a number, from 7 (July, when the season starts) through 5 (May, when it ends). Using R, filter the data to show only the end of each season, then export that CSV using `write_csv` and make a chart in Datawrapper comparing the three seasons for each age group. Have a title, description and source that tells readers about the data. The title and description should highlight the most newsworthy or important aspect.

HINT: In Datawrapper's "Check and Describe" tab, you can click on a column to get the option of "hiding" it in any visualization.

What do you think the story here is? Which age groups changed the most? Put the answer below along with the URL of your chart.

**A2.**

**Q3.** You want to know more about the geography of COVID-19 cases in Maryland in 2022, the year after vaccines became widely available. To do that, you'll make a choropleth map in Datawrapper. The `md_covid_cases_by_zip.csv` file has one row for each zip code and one column for each day of 2022, with the total number of cases reported in that zip code since the start of the pandemic. You will need to:

-   Read the file into R and create columns for the number of cases reported in each zip code *during 2022* (think about how to get that from two of the columns) and the percentage of all 2022 cases in the state that number represents and then export that CSV to use in your map.
-   Search for Maryland zip codes (use the 2020 zip codes) as the base map.
-   Upload the CSV file.
-   Change the tooltip to show both the number and the percentage (you can put them side by side or put one under the other). Make sure to properly format both numbers to make them readable.
-   Add labels to your map that locate prominent places in the state.
-   Have a title, description and source that tells readers about the data. The title and description should highlight the most newsworthy or important aspect.
-   Make any other changes to data that helps you make a more accurate map.

What do you think the story here is, and what would you want to know more about? What's the biggest limitation of mapping case counts this way? Put the answer below along with the URL of your map.
